newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral prepares to assume power.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral prepares to assume power.

text.p: India's United Front alliance staked a claim to form a new centre-left government on Sunday after its disparate parties formally elected prime minister-in-waiting Inder Kumar Gujral as their leader.
Parliamentarians from the 15-party alliance elected the 77-year-old Gujral as their leader, endorsing the choice late on Saturday of the alliance's decision-making Steering Committee.
"In this 50th year of our independence, I think we have a great deal to look back on and what we have accomplished," Gujral told his deputies in an emotional acceptance speech.
"Even more than that we have to make a new promise to the future, which Jawaharlal Nehru had called once the tryst with destiny. I think that tryst we have now got to revive again."
He was referring to the words of India's first prime minister, who spoke of the nation's tryst with destiny in August 1947 when the country won its freedom from Britain.

After the elections of Gujral, leaders of the alliance met President Shankar Dayal Sharma and staked a claim for him to succeed caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda. Gujral was not among the United Front leaders who met Sharma.
Alliance leader Chnadrababu Naidu told reporters he expected Sharma to invite Gujral later on Sunday to head the government.
"We have staked a claim to form the government," Naidu said. "We are hopeful of forming the government very soon."
Asked when Sharma would invite the United Front to form a new government, he said: "We are expecting to be called today."

Naidu, who spearheaded the efforts on Friday and Saturday to find a consensus United Front candidate, said he had asked caretaker Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) to reconsider its decision, announced on Saturday, not to join the government.

Gujral's election by his coalition's lawmakers was marred by the absence of deputies from the TMC. The TMC was upset that its leader G.K. Moopanar had been passed over in the selection of a new prime minister, coalition officials said.
The departure of the TMC meant Chidambaram, architect of a pathbreaking budget due to be taken up by parliament on Monday, would not be in Gujral's government.
Asked to comment on the fate of the budget, Chidambaram told Reuters on Sunday: "I'm not going to talk about it. You should ask the new government."
Gujral said he would continue to try to improve relations with India's South Asian neighbours while defending an independent foreign policy.
Gujral, who was foreign minister in the outgoing government, told Reuters Television that he would pay keen attention to relations with the major world powers.
"As foreign minister, I have built some sort of a doctrine regarding neighbourly relations. That will continue to be my priority area," said Gujral.

During his 10 months as foreign minister in Deve Gowda's government, Gujral helped to seal a landmark water-sharing treaty with Bangladesh and open a fresh dialogue with India's longtime foe Pakistan.
"I am equally keen that our relations with the major world powers -- Europe, America, China, Russia -- continue to get my attention," he said.
Gujral, who has a reputation for honesty and integrity, promised a clean government and emphasised his roots in India's freedom struggle.

"I am a humble man, but I have been in politics since freedom struggle days and I cherish this," he told the United Front deputies, adding that social justice would be his main plank. "I will take full advantage of my grey hair," he said.
